method.name: Mixture of Experts
method.principle: Independent experts transform a whole-life evidence map before any task filtering; integration preserves cross-domain leverage, disagreement, falsifiers, and a separate downstream execution adapter.

experts.label: Whole-Life Systems Expert
experts.mission: Map the full portfolio of identity, body, cognition, relationships, work, finance, opportunity, and execution across multiple timescales.
assumptions: User-authored nodes express desired directions but not necessarily current outcomes.
A balanced portfolio needs explicit sacrifice because capacity is finite.
derivation: The hierarchy contains a 360-degree domain architecture, not merely a task queue.
Housing is the highest-consequence current convergence point across home, finance, administration, calendar, and likely family/work capacity.
A seasonal portfolio can preserve whole-life scope while temporarily concentrating capacity.
experts.proposal: Use the August 14 Home Base Transition as the temporary organizing center, maintain minimum viable continuity elsewhere, then select one post-close capability lane.
risks: The portfolio can become another planning artifact.
Sparse outcome evidence makes domain weights uncertain.
experts.falsified_by: A two-scale cadence adds planning but produces no observable evidence in body, agency, or role domains across two cycles.

experts.label: Behavior & Measurement Expert
experts.mission: Separate repeated behavior, unmeasured states, completed external outcomes, and aspirational narratives without inferring causes.
assumptions: Habit logs are evidence of recorded behavior, not a complete measure of lived behavior.
Task completion dates indicate recorded closure but not every external artifact.
derivation: Eleven dated closures across Housing, Maintenance, Taxes, and Parents trip show real but concentrated external follow-through.
Tax steps closed as a burst after a prior review predicted continued carryover, so simple stalled-item forecasts are unreliable.
The abstinence sequence is auto-checked and therefore cannot be treated as verified adherence.
experts.proposal: Use finite external workflows—trigger, checklist, confirmation, brief reflection—and measure return speed rather than requiring an unbroken daily chain.
risks: Logging gaps can be mistaken for absence.
A streak may not transfer across domains.
experts.falsified_by: The daily proof is logged but produces no meaningful state change, or logs diverge from independently observable outcomes.

experts.label: Identity & Options Expert
experts.mission: Translate self-authored identity, social, family, skill, and opportunity language into enacted roles and deliberate options.
assumptions: Identity language is a stated aspiration, not a diagnosis or fixed trait.
Completed family logistics provide one observable example of role enactment.
derivation: Parents-trip care, tax closure, maintenance, and Housing document progress are enacted stewardship signals.
The explicit FOMO/sacrifice node recognizes that not every valid arena can be active simultaneously.
experts.proposal: Anchor identity in reliable stewardship now, then choose one 30–90 day capability lane after the closing transition.
risks: A role choice may be selected for image rather than personal value.
Current relationship and work evidence is sparse.
experts.falsified_by: The selected arena does not produce an observable artifact or no longer matches the user’s stated priorities.

integration_gate: Complete whole-life evidence coverage map required before task filtering
At least four evidence classes and four materially analyzed domains required
At least two non-task evidence classes required
Tasks may implement but may not define the visible strategy
No unsupported psychological, medical, legal, or causal claims

evidence.label: August 14 Home Base Transition
evidence.summary: The Housing project body records an August 14 closing and document review; the schedule says “house document paperwork”; two Housing descendants were completed July 28. The user explicitly reactivated this scope as the immediate priority.

evidence.label: 360-degree life architecture
evidence.summary: The hierarchy explicitly spans exercise, diet, skill, identity, social, finances, work, quarter-scoped work, and strategy, with lead-domino and augmented-intelligence structures connecting them.

evidence.label: Expansive identity horizon
evidence.summary: User-authored records repeatedly target hope, power, superior cognition, social presence, main-character energy, and a broad life reset.

evidence.label: Large ambition and small-horizon rules coexist
evidence.summary: The system contains both colossal-target language and explicit rules for the next hour, one small task per day, one-hour blocks, and easy-mode-first progression; fixed deadline planning is recorded as not working so far.

evidence.label: Uneven and differently verified habit evidence
evidence.summary: The abstinence stream contains 24 consecutive auto-checked dates through July 28, exercise has nine manual entries ending July 8, and sleep/Taking action have zero entries. The auto-checked sequence does not independently verify adherence.

evidence.label: Vitality is distributed across many projects
evidence.summary: Brain, lifestyle, sexual health, lung, hair, exercise, sleep, diet, meditation, and rewire records form a broad vitality portfolio with more hypotheses than measured outcomes.

evidence.label: Strategy is richer than time allocation
evidence.summary: The schedule surface has one populated text cue and six blank entries, while the hierarchy contains 181 records and explicit next-hour and weekly-system ideas.

evidence.label: Family care has an external completion trace
evidence.summary: The completed Parents trip body records seats, wheelchair follow-up, check-in, connectivity, address/job information, and practice with the user’s father.

evidence.label: Eleven external closures across four domains
evidence.summary: Eleven now-in-scope native tasks carry completion dates: five Maintenance, three Taxes, two Housing, and one Parents trip; seven eligible tasks remain open elsewhere.

evidence.label: Social, skill, and work are designed but under-observed
evidence.summary: Social presence, communication, skill learning, work, fearlessness, and decision frameworks are explicit nodes, but the current mirror contains little outcome evidence for them.

evidence.label: Opportunity scanning lacks a consistent conversion path
evidence.summary: Braindump records include AI/startup research links and explicit systems for research→insight→action and practical mental-model digestion, but outcomes are not consistently linked back.

models.label: Multi-Timescale Control
models.source: extended: hierarchical control and temporal abstraction
models.role: Connect a large strategic reference state to next-hour actions and weekly feedback without collapsing one into the other.

models.label: Pareto Portfolio Design
models.role: Allocate finite capacity across life domains and make sacrifices explicit instead of pretending every valid goal can be active.

models.label: Bayesian Measurement
models.role: Distinguish observed logs and outcomes from unknown, unlogged, or aspirational states.

models.label: Exploration–Exploitation
models.role: Bound research and optimization while allocating enough effort to test one real-life intervention or role arena.

models.label: Option Value
models.source: stored: thinking in bets / real options
models.role: Activate one reversible arena while preserving other aspirations without turning them into simultaneous WIP.

models.label: Signaling Theory
models.role: Treat externally visible repeated behavior as stronger identity evidence than labels alone.

models.label: Feedback Control
models.role: End each small action with a measurable state and update the next choice without making task throughput the life strategy.

syntheses.title: Protect the Home Base Transition
syntheses.problem: The most consequential current commitment was hidden by retired metadata and has no eligible open native task, despite an August 14 closing, a schedule cue, and two July 28 document completions.
syntheses.solution: Make the Home Base Transition the temporary organizing center through closing: establish the authoritative outstanding checklist, dates, owners, financial/document readiness, and post-close stabilization needs. Preserve minimum viable continuity elsewhere.

context_applications.label: Whole-Life Systems
context_applications.application: Housing connects home base, finance, administration, calendar capacity, and likely family/work logistics; it is a convergence point rather than one paperwork item.
context_applications.decision_implication: Temporarily subordinate lower-consequence expansion work until closing readiness is externally verified.

context_applications.label: Behavior & Measurement
context_applications.application: Two Housing document steps are complete, but completion labels do not establish the remaining closing state.
context_applications.decision_implication: Obtain one authoritative checklist/status rather than infer readiness from completed descendants.

context_decision.choice: Make the August 14 Home Base Transition the immediate critical path.
context_decision.why: It has the highest documented consequence of delay and crosses several life domains.
context_decision.alternative: Continue the generic IRS/AR-11/internet queue while Housing remains implicit; that would optimize available task metadata instead of consequence.
context_decision.review: Reverse only if the transaction is cancelled, already closed, or the date materially changes.

context_actions.label: Establish authoritative closing readiness
context_actions.move: Collect the lender/attorney/closing-party checklist, exact outstanding states, dates, owners, funds/documents, and calendar constraints.
context_actions.done_when: One authoritative source shows what is complete, what remains, who owns each item, and when it is due.

syntheses.disagreement: The project metadata implied retirement, while body, schedule, recent completions, and the user’s explicit override establish current consequence. Substance now governs scope.

syntheses.title: Return Quickly and Finish Finite Chains
syntheses.problem: The identity system favors an unbroken daily jet stream and legacy fixed allocation, while observed outcomes arrive in episodic finite workflows and fixed schedules are explicitly recorded as not working.
syntheses.solution: Use trigger → checklist → confirmation → brief reflection as the operating unit. Preserve the large direction, but judge continuity by rapid return and attributable states rather than an unbroken chain or rigid hourly plan.

context_applications.label: Behavior & Measurement
context_applications.application: Parents trip and Taxes show sequential closure chains; the July tax burst followed a review that expected continued carryover.
context_applications.decision_implication: Design for recoverable bursts and record activation conditions before claiming a universal daily mechanism.

context_applications.label: Whole-Life Systems
context_applications.application: Colossal targets can orient the system while one small task, next-hour thinking, and easy-mode-first control the immediate interval.
context_applications.decision_implication: Separate strategic direction from the small control unit instead of forcing one scale to do both jobs.

context_decision.why: It matches observed bursty closure and the user’s small-unit rules without lowering ambition.
context_decision.alternative: Add another rigid schedule or interpret a missed day as system failure.
context_decision.review: Keep if separate closure sessions recur and context survives between them.

context_actions.label: One bounded external workflow
context_actions.move: Advance AR-11 only after the Housing closing state is visible.
context_actions.done_when: A confirmation, exact requirement, or exact blocker exists.

context_actions.label: Honor a recorded feedback interval
context_actions.move: Recheck IRS on or after the one-week interval recorded July 28.
context_actions.done_when: A dated status or exact next requirement exists.

syntheses.disagreement: Daily-chain language motivates continuity, but auto-checked habits and episodic outcomes do not verify a daily behavioral mechanism. Rapid return is the safer operational hypothesis.

syntheses.title: Seasonal Concentration, Whole-Life Preservation
syntheses.problem: The system represents nearly every life domain and legacy schedules allocate 75 nominal hours weekly, while current work/skill/social outcomes and actual time use are under-observed.
syntheses.solution: Use one seasonal emphasis—Housing now—while maintaining simple foundations and preserving other domains as inactive options. After stabilization, select one 30–90 day capability lane from health, work, skill, social, identity, or problem solving.

context_applications.label: Identity & Options
context_applications.application: Reliable stewardship is already visible through family coordination, maintenance, Taxes, and Housing documents; this is stronger present identity evidence than deficit labels.
context_applications.decision_implication: Build identity from enacted stewardship now; choose a capability lane after the transition.

context_applications.label: Whole-Life Systems
context_applications.application: The FOMO/sacrifice node supplies the allocation rule the 360-degree architecture lacks.
context_applications.decision_implication: Name the seasonal emphasis and the domains receiving minimum viable continuity.

context_decision.choice: Use Housing as the seasonal emphasis and postpone selection of one growth lane until closing stability is visible.
context_decision.why: This protects consequence without shrinking the whole-life map to administration.
context_decision.alternative: Run every bucket simultaneously or treat administration as the permanent life strategy.
context_decision.review: Select the next lane after closing readiness/stabilization or sooner if a higher-consequence event emerges.

context_actions.label: Select one post-close capability lane
context_actions.move: After the transition is stable, choose one health, work, skill, social, identity, or problem-solving lane with an observable outcome.
context_actions.done_when: One lane, one outcome, one review signal, and explicit sacrifices are named.

syntheses.disagreement: Whole-life scope argues for domain coverage; finite capacity argues for concentration. Seasonal allocation preserves both.

decisions.label: Protect the August 14 transition
decisions.rationale: Housing is the highest-consequence documented commitment and was hidden by stale scope metadata.
decisions.tradeoff: Lower-consequence tasks and exploration become subordinate.
decisions.review: Reverse if the closing is cancelled, complete, or materially rescheduled.

decisions.label: Use finite closure chains
decisions.rationale: Observed completion is bursty and sequential; rigid scheduling is explicitly recorded as ineffective.
decisions.tradeoff: The unbroken-chain identity is replaced by rapid return and attributable closure.
decisions.review: Keep only if closure sessions recur and context survives between them.

decisions.label: Concentrate seasonally
decisions.rationale: Whole-life ambition needs one temporary emphasis plus minimum viable continuity elsewhere.
decisions.tradeoff: Most valid domains remain inactive options during closing.
decisions.review: Choose the next capability lane after closing stabilization.

position.headline: Protect the August 14 home-base transition—and use it as proof of the steward you are becoming.
position.summary: Your Outliner is a whole-life reconstruction architecture, but the decisive present reality is an August 14 Housing closing that connects home, finance, administration, time, and future stability. Recent Taxes, Parents trip, Maintenance, and two Housing document completions show a pattern of consequential stewardship—not universal paralysis. The strategy is to make closing reality authoritative, operate through finite closure chains and rapid return, preserve minimum viable continuity elsewhere, then direct the freed capacity into one chosen 30–90 day capability lane.
position.momentum: Eleven dated closures now span Housing, Maintenance, Taxes, and Parents trip; July shows bursty sequential follow-through rather than uniform daily execution.
position.tension: The highest-consequence commitment had stale retired metadata and no open native task, while abundant identity and scheduling architecture could distract from closing reality.
position.leverage: Turn Housing into a temporary whole-life convergence point, then convert demonstrated stewardship into one deliberately chosen growth lane.
position.confidence: High that Housing is the immediate organizing center after the user override; medium on post-close lane selection because work, skill, social, and actual-time evidence remain sparse.

evidence_balance.summary: All 181 records were enumerated before action filtering. The board integrates project bodies, hierarchy, habits, schedule, notes, links/tags, completed trajectory, and task state across nine domains; Housing is active by explicit user override despite stale metadata.
omitted_domains: Partner/friendship outcomes are not represented in the exposed data
Actual time use, current work outcomes, and external closing artifacts remain unavailable
Unknown agent-note contexts and binary attachments remain unavailable through the API

winning_moves.title: Make August 14 closing readiness authoritative
winning_moves.move: Build one source of truth for every remaining Housing item, owner, date, fund/document requirement, and calendar constraint; protect it above generic queue order.
winning_moves.why_now: Housing is the highest-consequence documented transition and was hidden only because metadata lagged reality.
unlocks: A stable home base for future growth
winning_moves.tradeoff: Lower-consequence administration and optimization remain subordinate until readiness is verified.
winning_moves.win_condition: A closing party confirms readiness or every remaining item has an owner, due date, and verified next state.

winning_moves.title: Return quickly and finish the next finite chain
winning_moves.move: Use trigger → checklist → confirmation → brief reflection. Judge momentum by attributable states and return speed, not a never-miss chain or a rigid hourly plan.
winning_moves.why_now: Parents trip, Taxes, Maintenance, and Housing show sequential closure bursts; fixed schedules are recorded as not working, and the apparent abstinence streak is auto-checked.
unlocks: A mechanism grounded in observed outcomes
winning_moves.tradeoff: You give up the emotionally clean story that momentum must look uniform every day.
winning_moves.win_condition: Two separate closure sessions reach verified external states and leave a clear next-state record.

winning_moves.title: Use seasonal concentration without shrinking your life
winning_moves.move: Let Housing be the temporary emphasis. Preserve simple health, work, and relationship continuity; after stabilization, select one capability lane and explicitly keep the others as options.
winning_moves.why_now: The 360-degree map is valuable for coverage but legacy allocation exceeds observed capacity and outcome evidence.
winning_moves.tradeoff: Most valid aspirations remain consciously inactive during the transition.
winning_moves.win_condition: Home base is stabilized and one capability lane has an observable outcome, review signal, and named sacrifices.

hidden_leverage.title: Stewardship is already stronger identity evidence than deficit labels
hidden_leverage.insight: Family coordination, taxes, maintenance, and Housing documents show reliability under consequence; these records coexist with self-critical power/status language.
hidden_leverage.why_it_matters: You can build agency from demonstrated care and stewardship now rather than waiting to feel cognitively or socially “fixed.”
hidden_leverage.mechanism: Signaling theory weights costly, externally consequential behavior more than aspiration labels.
hidden_leverage.falsifier: The completion states lack external outcomes or the stewardship pattern does not recur.

hidden_leverage.title: Your effective rhythm may be sequential bursts, not daily uniformity
hidden_leverage.insight: Taxes closed as a linked cluster after a review expected carryover; Parents trip also used a finite checklist. The data supports episodic closure, not yet a universal daily habit mechanism.
hidden_leverage.why_it_matters: Designing for rapid return can preserve ambition without treating a missed day as identity failure.
hidden_leverage.mechanism: Feedback control preserves next-state continuity across interrupted control intervals.
hidden_leverage.falsifier: Separate closure sessions do not recur or context records fail to improve re-entry.

hidden_leverage.title: Big direction and small control are complementary
hidden_leverage.insight: Colossal targets can orient the season while the next hour, one small task, and easy-mode-first govern immediate execution.
hidden_leverage.why_it_matters: You do not need to choose between ambition and small steps; you need each at its correct timescale.
hidden_leverage.mechanism: Multi-timescale control separates reference state from immediate control action.
hidden_leverage.falsifier: The two-scale structure increases planning overhead or produces no attributable progress.

hidden_leverage.title: Housing can consolidate more than paperwork
hidden_leverage.insight: A successful home-base transition can reduce uncertainty across finance, administration, calendar, environment, and future planning—if post-close stabilization is included.
hidden_leverage.why_it_matters: The closing is a whole-life state transition, not merely a document deadline.
hidden_leverage.mechanism: Pareto portfolio design concentrates temporary capacity where one outcome affects several domains.
hidden_leverage.falsifier: The transaction is inactive or stabilization produces no meaningful reduction in cross-domain uncertainty.

pivot_signals.signal: A closing professional confirms the August 14 transaction and names outstanding requirements.
pivot_signals.meaning: Housing remains the immediate critical path with an evidence-backed sequence.
pivot_signals.response: Execute and track that checklist above lower-consequence queue items.

pivot_signals.signal: The closing is cancelled, complete, or materially rescheduled.
pivot_signals.response: Remove Housing from immediate priority and re-rank the portfolio from current evidence.

pivot_signals.signal: Two separate finite workflows reach externally verified states.
pivot_signals.meaning: Rapid-return continuity is reproducing beyond one burst.
pivot_signals.response: Keep the workflow unit and cautiously transfer it to the chosen capability lane.

pivot_signals.signal: Professional evidence establishes medical urgency or long lead time.
pivot_signals.meaning: A health path now has greater decision value than its task wording alone provided.
pivot_signals.response: Advance that health question and deliberately defer a lower-consequence lane.

pivot_signals.signal: Post-close capacity is materially lower or higher than expected.
pivot_signals.meaning: The feasible 30–90 day portfolio has changed.
pivot_signals.response: Resize minimum viable continuity and select the capability lane using actual capacity.

reasoning_provenance.summary: The verified whole-life map was analyzed before task filtering, independently challenged by three reviewers, corrected for auto-checked habit evidence, and updated after the user explicitly reactivated Housing.
reasoning_provenance.evidence_scope: Verified 181-node mirror: 163 non-task nodes, 18 task nodes, 10 attached bodies, 11 projects, four habit streams with verification metadata, ten notes, schedule, eight tags, native links, 11 in-scope completions, and prior-snapshot delta.
uncertainty: The external closing checklist and actual readiness are not mirrored.
Actual time use and current work/social outcomes are sparse.
Auto-checked habit dates do not independently verify adherence.
Unknown note contexts and binary attachments cannot be enumerated through the API.
